briefdescription.para: Owned configuration sections, populated once at construction.
Default-constructs every configuration section (each reads the environment).
Virtual destructor; derived configurators may extend the section set.
Logs the values of the nine non-test configuration sections.

detaileddescription.para:
Delegates to each section's printValues(). Secret-bearing fields (database password, token secret) are logged as "[redacted]"; the token secret additionally triggers a warning while it still equals the shipped default. The test-only Testing section is deliberately not printed.
Diagnostic output only; no validation or mutation is performed.

briefdescription.para: Returns the configuration section of type T.

parameterdescription.para: A section type satisfying Config; explicit specializations in configurator.cpp map each supported type to its member.

simplesect.para: Reference to the corresponding section member.
Only the ten specialized types are retrievable; instantiating get<T>() for any other Config type compiles but fails to link.
The returned reference is mutable and unsynchronized; do not modify it after construction.

briefdescription.para: Owning aggregate of all runtime configuration sections.

detaileddescription.para: Holds one instance per configuration domain (server, database, DoS detection, tokens, frontend, email sender, caches and workers) plus a testing section. Every section derives from EnvLoader and reads its values from the process environment in its constructor, falling back to the constants in the Defaults namespace when a variable is absent or invalid. The Configurator is intended to be a single process-wide object owned by Store and fully constructed before the Drogon IO threads start; sections are retrieved by type through get<T>().

simplesect.para: Values are snapshotted at construction time, so later changes to the environment do not affect an already-built Configurator.
get() returns a non-const reference and performs no locking. Treat sections as read-only once construction is complete; unsynchronized concurrent mutation is unsafe.
